A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LWM research, authors, model family and training approach. Their complete text, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original results for its trained models, including needle retrieval, MT-Bench, image and video understanding, generation examples and training ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains original model evaluations and ablations and additionally reports LWM results on LOFT and Video-MME.

M1.justification: The Llama-2 7B architecture, progressive context extension, RoPE scaling, synthetic QA construction, VQGAN tokenization, masked packing, loss weighting and generation procedure remain unchanged. The redrawn architecture diagram and suggested future use of CLIP embeddings do not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: v4 adds natural long-context tasks from LOFT: Quora duplicate detection, HotpotQA document retrieval and NQ retrieval-based question answering. It also adds medium and long Video-MME evaluation. Conversely, VisWiz, TextVQA and MM-Vet coverage disappears from the reported evaluations; POPE remains in the packing ablation. Training dataset coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The multi-needle comparison adds Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3. LOFT introduces GPT-4o and Claude 3 Opus comparisons, while Video-MME adds several newer video comparators. Video-LLaVA is removed from the retained short-video benchmark comparison, although it remains in long-video and qualitative comparisons.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include LOFT with LWM at 512K context versus baselines labeled 128K and 200K, and Video-MME comparisons stratified by duration with model-specific frame budgets. New needle baselines are evaluated through positional extrapolation to longer contexts. Short-video reporting drops the separate Score metric. Existing LWM training settings remain unchanged; newly disclosed qualitative-video preprocessing is documentation rather than an established protocol revision.

E4.justification: The added positional-extrapolation comparisons extend evidence about shorter-context models' robustness at lengths up to 1M tokens. The existing masked-packing and chat/QA-mixture ablations are retained in Appendix B, and the qualitative cases are retained. LOFT and Video-MME otherwise add benchmark evaluations rather than new ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for these evaluations. v4 continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v4 adds LWM LOFT scores of 0.38, 0.37 and 0.72 for Quora, NQ and HotpotQA, and Video-MME scores of 63.7 and 60.8 for medium and long videos. These are new evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v3. New comparator rows and removed visual benchmark entries substantially change the result set. Common table entries remain unchanged, but the N=2, R=2 bar at 223K changes from approximately 0.80 in v3 Figure 6 to 0.70 in v4 Figure 5.

T1.justification: No formal theorem, proof, derivation or mathematical assumption is added or revised. The attention-complexity and positional-scaling rationale remains substantively unchanged; Appendix D elaborates the existing needle task rather than introducing new theory.

C1.justification: v4 emphasizes the development process for long-context language and video-language models and narrows the introduction's claim from 'by far the best results ever reported' to 'competitive results.' The conclusion drops the explicit 'largest to date' assertion. The central contributions of million-token models, training techniques and open implementation remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds an explicit warning that findings from 7B models may not transfer to 100B-plus models and proposes continuous visual embeddings as a remedy for vision limitations. It removes v3's explicit caveat about inaccurate answers and difficulty with higher-level video questions, along with the future-work discussion of additional modalities and better video data. Existing chat/retrieval trade-off interpretations remain.

D1.justification: New Appendices D and G document multi-needle answer extraction and string matching, and qualitative-video evaluation at 1 FPS with uniform frame limiting and resizing/center cropping to 256 by 256. These disclose details of retained evaluations without establishing changed procedures. Training hyperparameters, hardware, budgets and inference sharding are retained, largely relocated.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to world-model work by Ha and Schmidhuber and Brooks et al., plus LOFT, Video-MME and HotpotQA. It removes several references supporting retained baseline names and the Rabe–Staats attention citation. The discussion newly emphasizes compatibility with continuous visual embeddings, while the principal context-extension and instruction-tuning positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion and substantial explanatory passages are rewritten. v4 removes the contents page, consolidates Stage I subsections, reorders language evaluations, moves Further Details and existing ablations into appendices, and adds summary/takeaway boxes. This substantially changes the narrative structure independently of the new experiments.

P2.justification: v4 adds a context-size comparison figure and new benchmark tables, redraws the architecture diagram, and reformats the retrieval comparison, including its legend and horizontal-axis label. It merges and reduces the image/short-video tables, relocates training tables and several figures to appendices, and revises numerous captions and page layouts. Most qualitative imagery is retained.

improvement.justification: LOFT and Video-MME strengthen evidence for the central long-context capabilities beyond v3's synthetic retrieval and selected video examples. Newer comparators and evaluation details also improve assessability. These gains are tempered by unequal context/frame budgets, removal of weak visual benchmark results and the strongest short-video comparator, and loss of the explicit complex-video failure caveat. Overall, the evidence supports a useful but limited quality improvement.
